title: Editor menu customization
summary: Rename the Edit menu to Editor, remove history commands from that menu, and add persisted appearance, assistant settings, and toolbox customization surfaces.

questions.question: Should Assistant Settings permit unrestricted prompt/tool authoring?
questions.decision: Keep provider/model management; allow an additional user instruction without replacing Zakape's safety envelope; toggle built-in skills and function tools only; reject arbitrary native commands, executable code, unrestricted network tools, and model-defined functions; include Restore defaults.

questions.question: Should Appearance follow operating-system theme changes?
questions.decision: Offer explicit Dark and Light modes only; never change an explicit choice because the operating-system theme changes.

questions.question: Should settings save continuously or transactionally?
questions.decision: Use live draft preview with Apply, Cancel, and Restore defaults; only Apply persists and Cancel restores the last applied state.

questions.question: What does hiding a toolbox item mean for keyboard access?
questions.decision: Pencil, Eraser, and Hand remain visible; optional tools may be hidden and reordered; hidden tools remain available through existing shortcuts.

questions.question: Where do preferences belong?
questions.decision: Preferences are device-local and shared across guest/local sessions; they are excluded from project files and exports and are not account-synchronized or exportable in this scope.

questions.question: Should accent editing be preset-only or arbitrary?
questions.decision: Provide curated accent presets plus a custom color-picker/hex value; derive hover, focus, muted, and contrast-safe variants and reject colors that cannot remain readable in the selected theme.

questions.question: How should model and assistant configuration be presented?
questions.decision: One tabbed Assistant Settings modal owns Model, Instructions, Skills, and Tools; existing model-management entry points open its Model tab.

questions.question: Which assistant capabilities may be disabled?
questions.decision: Require at least one enabled skill and keep the essential pixel-writing function enabled; layer, frame, timing, fill, and transform functions may be toggled off.

questions.question: How should future tools interact with a customized toolbox?
questions.decision: New optional tools appear as New and disabled without disturbing the user's order; preference migrations may insert future mandatory core tools.

dependencies.reason: The completed shared desktop/touch ApplicationMenu architecture is the menu surface being extended.

risks: Literal dark colors can leave unreadable or visually inconsistent islands in the new light theme.
An arbitrary accent can fail contrast or spread into neutral surfaces and recreate an over-tinted interface.
Asynchronous preference hydration can cause a visible dark-to-light startup flash or stale cache race.
Live appearance preview or draft connection testing can leak cancelled values into applied state.
Refactoring model settings can accidentally persist API keys that are currently session-only.
Filtering assistant tools only in the prompt can still allow a model response to execute a disabled capability.
An empty skill set or disabled pixel-writing capability can make the assistant accept work it cannot perform.
New, retired, duplicate, or malformed tool IDs can corrupt a customized rail order after upgrades.
Hiding the active optional tool can leave an invisible active state or inaccessible canvas interaction.
Drag-only ordering and tall tabbed dialogs can fail on touch, keyboard, short viewports, and safe-area devices.
Preference write failures can be mistaken for project persistence failures or unexpectedly mutate artwork state.
Allowing custom executable assistant tools would expand native and model trust boundaries beyond this specification.
validation: Unit-test appearance parsing, contrast thresholds, semantic token derivation, startup cache reconciliation, invalid fallback, and transactional rollback.

Unit-test assistant/toolbox v1 normalization, required capabilities/core tools, unknown/duplicate/retired/new IDs, stable ordering, bounded instructions, tool mapping, draft connection tests, and API-key non-persistence.
Adversarially test that disabled assistant actions and operations are omitted from requests and rejected from model responses while the protected prompt and proposal-review boundary remain active.

Playwright-test desktop and touch Editor menus, retained Undo/Redo shortcuts, all settings Apply/Cancel/default flows, reload persistence, model-tab routing, tool reordering, hidden-tool shortcuts, fallback behavior, and project-state neutrality.

Perform accessibility and responsive checks for semantic dialogs, focus containment/return, error announcements, 42-pixel coarse-pointer targets, non-drag ordering, safe areas, constrained heights, reduced motion, and horizontal overflow.
Review desktop, phone, and tablet screenshots in dark and light themes across Home, editor, menus, drawers, dialogs, glass panels, canvas chrome, hover/focus/disabled states, and custom accents.
Run affected-file Prettier, studio lint/typecheck/unit/build, focused/full Playwright, root spec tests and validation, pnpm spec validate UI-49ZB, and git diff --check.
validationEvidence: Implemented Editor menu customization: Appearance, bounded Assistant Settings, and Toolbox Editor with device-local transactional preferences. Studio lint, typecheck, 15 unit files/73 tests, production build, focused desktop/touch Playwright flows, spec validation, and git diff --check pass.
